summary:
South Sulawesi is a province of Indonesia and stands under the national legal framework, which applies here in full.

OutRight Action International's 2022 report Creeping Criminalisation, by Katjasungkana and Wieringa, lists South Sulawesi among the eight Indonesian provinces it covers and records that provincial and city bylaws in these jurisdictions criminalise same-sex conduct and gender nonconformity, adopted under the regional-autonomy powers that let local legislatures pass their own regulations.

In Makassar, the mayor reaffirmed in April 2025 a commitment to push an anti-LGBT regional regulation (Perda) after a same-sex act at a night-entertainment venue circulated online. The deputy chair of the city legislature's law-drafting body (Bapemperda) backed the move, saying the regulation was needed to preserve moral and religious norms.

The proposal is not new. It entered the 2023 local legislative programme (prolegda) as a priority for discussion, and two city legislature members, including Azwar ST of the PKS faction, said it was modelled on regulations already passed elsewhere, such as Bogor. As of April 2026 the Makassar rule remained a draft (Ranperda) rather than an enacted regulation.

Official posture in the city has hardened independently of the draft's status. The Makassar city government's women's-empowerment and child-protection agency (DP3A) is running an LGBT "prevention" programme, and a city legislature member, Muchlis Misbah, backs the pending Ranperda on HIV/AIDS and LGBT as legal reinforcement.
tangentialFactors:
Constitutional-law expert Bivitri Susanti characterises such local regulations as a trend ahead of the political year that risks worsening discrimination and persecution of LGBT people, and notes that the central government does little to stop discriminatory local regulations.

The Bogor comparison places Makassar's proposal inside a wider set of municipal anti-LGBT regulations rather than an isolated local initiative.

The 2022 report's account of provincial and city bylaws criminalising same-sex conduct and gender nonconformity in South Sulawesi sits alongside the Makassar regulation reported between 2023 and 2026, which remains a draft; the available reporting does not reconcile the two or identify which local bylaws are in force.
localsOnly:
The Makassar women's-empowerment and child-protection agency (DP3A) is intensifying LGBT "prevention" through socialization and education aimed at school-age children, alongside case handling with counselling and a safe house for people reported to it. DP3A head Ita Isdiana Anwar says most reports come from worried families.

A Komisi D monitoring meeting showed rising LGBT numbers alongside HIV/AIDS cases, and city legislature member Muchlis Misbah cites that finding in backing the pending Ranperda on HIV/AIDS and LGBT as legal reinforcement.

As of April 2026 the Makassar rule remains proposed (Ranperda) rather than enacted, so the city's current work rests on administrative programmes rather than a local criminal provision of its own.
outOfScopeNotes:
No South Sulawesi bylaw is identified in the available reporting as enacted and in force, and no prosecution or enforcement action under a South Sulawesi or Makassar regulation is recorded.

The 2023 prolegda entry predates the April 2025 mayoral reaffirmation; the outcome of the 2023 discussion and the text of any draft are not sourced.

No region-specific data on violence against trans people, police conduct, or access to care in South Sulawesi appears in the available reporting.
